comparison: Strong agreement on I3A's therapeutic effects on NAFLD parameters (C7-C12, C35-C39, C46, C128). Both evaluations find the data convincing with dose-dependent improvements in hepatic steatosis, inflammation, ALT, triglycerides, and histological scoring. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and dose-response relationships, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the convincing nature of the findings.

Strong agreement on microbiome findings (C13, C56-C66, C141). Both evaluations accept that I3A produces hepatoprotective effects without altering gut microbiome composition. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of multiple analytical approaches (α-diversity, β-diversity, LEfSe, PCA), while peer reviewers acknowledge this as a strength supporting direct host tissue effects.

Strong agreement on metabolomic changes (C15, C67-C79). Both evaluations support dose-dependent metabolomic alterations with I3A treatment. OpenEval details PLS-DA analysis and pathway enrichment showing tryptophan metabolite restoration, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm I3A rescued WD-altered metabolome as a major strength.

Strong agreement on proteomic changes (C16, C80-C86). Both evaluations support dose-dependent proteomic alterations showing partial reversal toward control levels. OpenEval emphasizes statistical testing and dose-response patterns, while peer reviewers accept the proteome rescue findings without methodological concerns.

Agreement on lipogenesis pathway effects (C17, C87-C90, C146-C147, C149). Both evaluations support selective targeting of Fasn without CD36 modulation. OpenEval provides detailed proteomics data showing 86% Fasn reduction, while peer reviewers accept reduced de novo lipogenesis enzyme levels as part of overall metabolic effects.

Agreement on β-oxidation enzyme modulation (C18, C91-C97). Both evaluations support I3A's effects on reducing mitochondrial β-oxidation enzymes. OpenEval provides targeted proteomics showing significant decreases in all four enzymes, while peer reviewers accept reduced β-oxidation as part of I3A's metabolic effects without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on AMPK-mediated anti-inflammatory mechanism (C19, C106-C127, C189-C190, C197). Both evaluations support AMPK as a key mediator. OpenEval details convergent evidence from p-AMPK restoration, AICAR activation, and siRNA knockdown experiments, while peer reviewers explicitly list AMPK-dependent anti-inflammatory activity as a major strength.

Perfect agreement on weight-independent effects (C40-C41, C130-C132). Both evaluations accept that I3A's hepatoprotective effects occur independently of body weight or caloric intake changes. OpenEval emphasizes this rules out indirect obesity effects, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging the finding.

Agreement on bile acid profile changes (C42-C43, C50-C52). Both evaluations support statistically significant bile acid alterations. OpenEval notes species-specific limitations affecting translational relevance, while peer reviewers accept bile acid reversal as part of overall metabolic improvements without questioning species differences.

Agreement on iron metabolism protein changes (C102-C105). Both evaluations accept dose-dependent effects on hepcidin and serotransferrin. OpenEval notes statistical significance but questions functional relevance for NAFLD, while peer reviewers accept as supporting mechanistic data without critique.

Agreement on antioxidant enzyme modulation (C99, C162-C163). Both evaluations support that CAT and GPx are downregulated by I3A treatment. OpenEval links this to reduced β-oxidation and ROS generation, while peer reviewers accept as consistent with overall metabolic effects.

OpenEval evaluated I3A pharmacokinetics (C29-C33) showing successful modulation of I3A levels across multiple compartments (feces, liver, serum), establishing the basis for therapeutic effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this is foundational data that peer reviewers likely accepted implicitly.

OpenEval rated liver FFA findings as UNCERTAIN (C53-C55) due to non-significant trend (p=0.11) for I3A effect despite 36% reduction magnitude. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address this uncertainty, possibly accepting the trend as part of overall metabolic improvements or not scrutinizing the statistical threshold.

OpenEval rated IL-10 findings as UNCERTAIN (C44-C45, C135) due to paradoxical upregulation by WD and downregulation by I3A, with speculative interpretation lacking mechanistic support. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address this counterintuitive finding or its interpretation.

OpenEval evaluated the interpretation of direct host tissue effects (C14, C143, C186, C191) as SUPPORTED based on absence of microbiome changes, while noting reliance on negative evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this interpretation through R2 but did not separately evaluate the inferential logic.

Peer reviewers accepted AhR mechanism in hepatocytes vs. AMPK in macrophages (C106-C109) as supporting cell-type-specific mechanisms. OpenEval included these claims in R8 focused on AMPK mechanism but did not separately evaluate the AhR/cell-type specificity interpretation.
